$comment: Rule Constitution R0/R6 made mechanical (seeded 2026-07-26). Every governance rule names the file+marker that ENFORCES it and the test file+marker whose removal turns the suite RED. test/rule-manifest.test.js is the lint: an entry whose markers vanish fails the build, so a rule can no longer be silently unwired. A rule with no mechanical enforcement yet MUST carry acknowledgedGap (an explicit, visible debt) — omitting both fails the lint. Grow this file with every new rail.

rules.rule: A denied board write is never silent: it is audited, returned to the caller, and push-notified to the operator.

redTest.mustContain: every denial audit collects a matching in-band denial

rules.rule: A card the operator froze is never completed over the freeze, even when the freeze postdates the run's start.

redTest.mustContain: a fresh frozen check precedes the pipeline board-complete

rules.rule: Autonomous handoff children are created blocked; a human (or the gate's safe-verb audit) releases them, never the proposing engine.

redTest.mustContain: handoff children are created blocked (human-gated), never todo/queued

rules.rule: The task gate is lexical and fail-closed: only a clearly safe leading verb with no gated keyword anywhere auto-runs; everything else waits for a human.
The social-posting exception neutralizes ONLY content verbs; every destructive/infra/credential keyword still hard-gates inside a social task.

redTest.mustContain: social exception invariant: each dangerous keyword still gates inside a social task

rules.rule: A sandboxed engine's child env carries only {PATH,HOME,(TERM/LANG)} plus its one inference credential — never the box's other secrets.
The autonomous read-jail chroot contains only allowlisted roots; home and secret paths are absent, not merely read-only.
Autonomous chains stop at hard ceilings (runs/time/tokens/dollars) with a soft zone at 80%; the gate enforces this, engines only self-throttle.
Watchers and dashboards reuse the live in-path enforcement predicates, never a parallel copy that can drift.
Gemini has no shell and no board read path; it never states board contents from memory — it says it cannot read the board and hands the read to an engine that can (Claude/Hermes in chat).

enforcedBy.mustContain: Gemini: you cannot read the board

rules.acknowledgedGap: The markers pin the charter text and its test, but the behavior itself is prose-governed: no code inspects a Gemini reply for fabricated board claims. Mechanical option (future): the gate cross-checks task ids Gemini cites against the live board and flags unknown/archived ids.

rules.rule: Every in-box claim acquired before the current machine boot is reaped exactly once at store construction, regardless of remaining TTL, before any scheduler tick; external claims and claims acquired after boot stay quarantined and fail-closed.
rules.source: launch-morning deadlock 2026-07-27 (four reboots, four zombie claims, dispatcher denied every 30s)

redTest.mustContain: unexpired two-hour in-box claim from before machine boot is reaped

rules.rule: Before editing the box's repo clone, an engine must fetch and fast-forward it to origin/main, stopping if the clone holds local work.
rules.acknowledgedGap: Prose-only: the charter instructs, but no code forces the sync before an edit lands. Mechanical option (future): the gate's git-ladder commit path refuses to commit in a clone that is behind origin.

rules.rule: The agent's writable terminal never listens on a network port. It binds a UNIX socket owned by agent and the boxstate group inside a 0750 dir, so the kernel gates who may type as the agent, and no credential is ever placed in argv (/proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable).
rules.source: ttyd credential hole found 2026-07-27 (launch day), reported by the box

redTest.mustContain: ttyd listens on a permissioned UNIX socket
